title: authoritative-participant-defeats-intended-unlinkability

proposition.statement: A relying system must not assert an unlinkability or minimization property without testing whether identifiers, proof configuration, issuance cadence, renewal behavior, or other metadata controlled by an authoritative participant can recreate a cross-context correlator.

preconditions: The system claims or relies on a privacy property that interactions should remain unlinkable or minimally correlatable.
An issuer, registry, operator, or other authoritative participant controls metadata or lifecycle behavior visible across interactions.
The controlled values or behavior are not independently shown to preserve the declared privacy property.

trigger.statement: Authoritative participant choices create a stable or distinctive join across interactions while local credential and proof validation continue to succeed.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence identifying which participant controls each potentially correlating identifier, metadata field, proof choice, issuance event, or renewal behavior.
Cross-context evidence testing whether the combined issuer- or operator-controlled surfaces enable correlation.
Evidence defining the unlinkability or minimization property that the deployment claims to provide.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for unlinkability while issuer-controlled or operator-controlled metadata consistently links otherwise separate interactions.
Assessment assumes that an authoritative participant preserves privacy merely because that participant is authorized to issue or operate the relevant component.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the privacy/correlation tranche.
Research provenance: W3C VC Data Model Threat Model v2.1 privacy threats concerning correlation and deployment behavior; draft/work in progress, not corpus authority.
